A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. The changed layout and equation numbering do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian-to-Swiss-Roll and weather-prediction experiments, plus neural-model and colored-MNIST demonstrations in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Sections 5.1–5.2 and Appendices A and C.

M1.justification: The likelihood objective, log-sum-exp cost, Gaussian-mixture potential, training procedure, and conditional sampling remain unchanged. The fully neural parameterization and energy-based Algorithm 1 already appeared in v2 Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Gaussian-to-Swiss-Roll mapping, January-to-June meteorological prediction, and colored-MNIST digit translation with a 120-degree hue shift. No dataset, task, or input scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the small- and large-data Swiss-Roll experiments and weather comparisons. CNF and CNF (SS) are renamed CondNF and CondNF (SS), respectively.

E3.justification: The stated sample sizes, splits, model configurations, and evaluation metrics are retained. Weather's 500 unpaired samples, 192 paired samples, and 100 test pairs move from Section 5.2 to Appendix B.3. Newly reported colored-MNIST computation details do not establish a changed protocol.

E4.justification: The 16K-sample baseline sanity check, source-versus-target unpaired-data ablation, weather sample-size analysis, and Appendix A demonstrations are retained. Figure 3's added ground-truth panel redisplays existing evidence.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same uncertainty reporting. Neither version supplies additional run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical results, including the proposed method's LL of 20.5±0.09 and CFD of 7.21±0.04, and CGMM (SS)'s CFD of 7.17±0.07. The synthetic mappings, ablation findings, and colored-MNIST outputs are also retained.

T1.justification: Appendix D.2 inserts epsilon-dependent factors into Gaussian prefactors and corrects b_m(x) to a_m(x) in the quadratic expansion. Equation (2) changes the dual supremum to a maximum. The principal propositions and universal-approximation assumptions and proof remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The four central contributions remain the combined-data likelihood objective, inverse-EOT equivalence, tractable Gaussian-mixture solver, and universal approximation. The introduction newly highlights neural parameterization already described and claimed applicable in v2 Appendix A and Discussion.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 now explicitly describes the chosen inverse-EOT formulation as one of several application-specific formulations and qualifies advanced-solver extensions as conjectural future work. Section 6 broadens possible extensions to Schrödinger bridges and flow matching; existing scalability and EBM-instability limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly reports 10,000 iterations, a 2080 Ti GPU, and approximately 40 minutes for the existing colored-MNIST experiment. Other implementation and code-access information is substantially retained.

R1.justification: Sections 2.2, 4, and 6 add targeted context and citations concerning alternative inverse-OT formulations, contrastive learning, Schrödinger bridges, EBM training, and flow matching. The central positioning against existing semi-supervised domain-translation methods remains intact.

P1.justification: Parts of the introduction, OT background, inverse-OT connection, and discussion are rewritten or condensed. Terminology and affiliations are updated, while the overall Sections 1–6 and Appendices A–D organization remains intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from two columns to one, with a redesigned title/author block and substantial reflow of equations, figures, and tables. Figure 3 expands to include an existing ground-truth visualization, and several displays are resized or repositioned.

improvement.justification: v3 provides clearer context for the selected inverse-EOT formulation, makes the neural demonstration easier to compare with ground truth, and adds useful computation details for colored MNIST. These support modest gains in clarity and reproducibility. The empirical evidence and principal guarantees remain unchanged, and the local derivation edits do not fully resolve Gaussian-normalization inconsistencies in Appendix D.2.
